Great cafe and shop
Nov 2019
Of the 3 L'Usine in town, Le Loi is hands down my favorite!!! The ambiance is cool, relaxed and cozy at the same time. A great place for both couples and groups of friends. Great place for a quick bite or a work day.

On the weekends they serve a special brunch consisting of approximately 7 of the items on their menu which gives you an opportunity to try a variety. This is also very cheap (190.000).
I can highly recommend everything on the brunch platter, english breakfast, crab and avocado toast and especially their french toast!

For dinner they have both western and eastern food and I have not been disappointed by either.
Drinks menu is big and it's my favorite cappucino in town so far. I can highly recommend The Funky Spinach Mango Smoothie(now Spinach Mango Glow) and Blended juices (Saigon heat and Root Radiance).

I have come back multiple times by now and the staff is always very nice and helpful. 
To top it of there's a very nice store on the ground level selling clothes, shoes and other stuff and it's a great time walking around in it!

We were promptly seated on the 4th floor and what is interesting is that the interiors differ slightly from floor to floor, all of which is decked out and done up in very tasteful fashion - somewhat rustic, Asian and contemporary, all in the same venue.

This is a western establishment that serves up your usual brunch fare with certain dishes having a Vietnamese influence/ twist. While I can’t recall our orders, I do recall that some dishes took much longer than expected (a corned beef hash came after the other guests finished their meals) but the dishes were decently sized, tasty and generally affordable. They also have a decent range of desserts but we didn’t have the chance to try them on this visit.

They have a small retail area on the 2nd floor and this space sells largely Vietnamese products that are higher end and not your run-of-the-mill souvenirs. Items like chocolates, clothes, household display items, coffee, etc are available and make a good gift, if you’re willing to splurge (more than what you would spend at Ben Thanh).

l’Usine is a decent cafe to spend a lazy afternoon at, with a book or with good company. We enjoyed our visit and wouldn’t hesitate to recommend L’Usine if you’re looking for a decent quiet cafe in an otherwise busy and confusing city.

The freshly squeezed pomelo juice was also very satisfying considering the sweltering heat and dust outside - you can't go wrong with juice, though.

Ambience wise, I can see how this would be a hit with Instagrammers and hipsters. I have been coming to L'usine for nearly two years. It has been one of my favorite places to go for coffee, breakfast or lunch. However, I had such a terrible experience last night at the Le Loi location for Christmas Eve dinner that I will never give L'usine my business again.

My co-worker had booked a table for 16 more than a week before, yet when we got there the table was not big enough. This wasn't a huge deal as we squeezed in and made do. After ordering wine, we were informed that they did not have enough wine glasses and an employee was sent over to the Dong Khoi restaurant to pick up more. It took about 20-25 minutes to get the glasses. Again, our reservation was made over a week ago, so I don't understand why the restaurant wasn't prepared for our party. Also, the place was not that crowded except for one other large party, so by no means was the staff slammed with customers.

We then ordered a bottle of Prosecco that our waiter proceeded to open and pour despite the bottle not being chilled at all. I assume this was just a rookie mistake because our waiter is a trainee - but seriously, why throw a trainee to the wolves on a night like Christmas Eve when people are expecting a special dinner?

Now we come to the biggest problem of the night - I literally had to re-order my dinner four times because each time I ordered was informed that the restaurant didn't have that item in stock anymore. The table had a "festive menu" on that I was excited to order from, but when I gave the waiter my order he pointed to microscopic print at the bottom of the menu that said "at Dong Khoi location only." Why would you put out this menu on Christmas Eve if you have zero intention of serving that food? At the very least, don't be deceptive and put in large print that it's only at the other location.

I then ordered steak frites. The waiter came back and told me they were out of steak. I then ordered bbq chicken. The waiter came back and told me they were out of chicken. I then ordered fish & chips. The waiter came back and told me they were out of fish and chips. I finally just asked him "what the hell do you still have left?" and was told they just had some pasta dishes and lasagna. All of the items listed as mains were out of stock. So I ended up having lasagna for my Christmas dinner.

Never before have I been to a restaurant where I had to order four times because the place was out of food. Again, the restaurant was not very busy last night and they knew that our party was going to be there for more that a week. Why didn't they plan ahead and have adequate supplies? It is probably the most unacceptable experience I've had at a restaurant anywhere.

We received no apology from the staff. In my opinion, the staff was disinterested - it was hard to get their attention and at no point did anyone come to our table and ask us how the food was or ask if we wanted dessert. We spent a lot of money there last night and deserved to be treated better than we were. Again, I've gone to both locations many, many times over the past two years and have given them a lot of money with no dissatisfaction. That changed last night and now L'usine has lost a loyal customer. Bye-bye.

The restaurant is well appointed and well designed. Everything feels modern yet rustic and the ambiance is relaxed.

The menu has mostly Western items including pancakes, eggs on toast, mini burgers, sandwiches, salad and other items. Breakfast is served all day and they even have cupcakes.

I ordered pancakes, eggs on toast and bacon to try a variety of items. The pancakes were thick, dense patties (almost like a donut) and not as enjoyable. However, the eggs on toast were delicious. I also had a fruit smoothie called Cyclo made of mango, strawberry and orange that was quite good. I got a cupcake because I was craving baked goods, but unfortunately, it was not that good. 

However, I bet this place would be an awesome place to hang out for brunch, for the ambiance alone. 

I would definitely return.

Totally disappointed
Jun 2016 • Family
My party of 8 came to this restaurant on Sunday around 12 pm for brunch. Coming in, we had high expectations due to the high reviews off trip advisor and high praises from a friend who recommended us to the restaurant. Needless to say, we were extremely disappointed.

I'll start by listing the positive aspects of the restaurant. First off, it has a great atmosphere with modern decor. The food are presented in a very visually appealing way. They have an extensive menu that boasts a diverse selection of food that is both Western and Vietnamese. After staying in Vietnam for a whole month and having a diet that consists 90% of Vietnamese cuisine, it's a godsend to be able to eat a Western breakfast for a change. The portions are generous and the food is presented in a very visually appealing way.

All these positive aspects of the restaurant had us prepared for an awesome dining experience. However, that was exactly the opposite of our experience eating here.

Upon entering the restaurant, we were promptly seated and handed out menus. After perusing through the menu, our party of 8 were finally ready to place our orders. However, the waiters were nowhere to be found and it took another 5-10 minutes before we were able to grab one of their attentions. They could not be placed entirely at fault for this though because given the time and day we visited the restaurant, it was understandably busy and the staff had a lot of tables to attend to.

When the waitress finally came to take our orders, she addressed each of us one by one to ask for our order. She acknowledged everyone's order and repeated each one back to them prior to moving on to the next person. A detail I noticed was she did not write any of our orders down, which made me assume that she had the memory capacity of Rain Man.

After taking all of our orders, she returned to the front to enter in our orders. After a short amount of time, the food began coming out to all but two people of our table. The waiter assured us that the food will come out very soon. Rather than having everyone patiently wait for the two to receive their food, it was insisted that everyone begin digging in. After 5 minutes into everyone's meal, another plate came out and we were only waiting for one last person of the party to receive his food.

An additional 5 minutes passed by and we flagged down the waiter to ask for the ETA of the last party member's food. With a smile on his face, he assured us that it would be coming out very soon and he would go speak to the back. The reassurance kept our optimism high. Then, after everyone were 80% through their meal, we then asked the waiter one last time on the ETA of the plate. Now the previous assumption that I had of the waitress that took our order having Rain Man capabilities began to fade and now I had to ask whether the order was even written down for the last member of our party. He reassured us again that the food will be coming out immediately and returned to the back.

After another 2-3 minutes passed by, the waiter that had been reassuring us this whole time returns from the back with the order form and informs us that he took a gander (finally? I assume) through our order and discovered that the item we had been waiting on was never even written down. Without even apologizing, he then tells us "So I looked through the menu and I can't find the order. Did you want me to enter the order in now?"

After everyone had already eaten 90% of their meal?! Understandably, the member of our party that has been waiting anxiously for his food lost his appetite and no longer wanted the order. We were all outraged that the waitress had neglected to write down all the orders. There were 8 heads at the table and she only wrote down 7?!

After concluding our meal, we paid the bill and got up to leave. Before we left, the waitress that took our order was confronted and offered a suggestion: to please write down the customer's orders next time.

The conversation that unfolded was as presented (nearly verbatim):

Me: We are very disappointed. A member of our party did not receive his order. You should write down the orders next time.
Waitress: Oh.

There was not even an apology!

We are extremely disappointed and if our experience represented the typical experience of what the restaurant had to offer, then it does not deserve the high praise that it receives.

Tl;dr: Atmosphere is great. Food is decent, but not good enough to warrant you to clean off your plate. If you want a break from Vietnamese food and have a Western brunch, this place is probably it. Service was HORRIBLE.

Perfect on many levels
Jun 2015 • Solo
I love this place.

It is really hard to find and is not visible from the street. If you take a taxi here you will get dropped off at an art gallery. Walk through the gallery, take your first right and go up the stairs. There you will find this gem of a place.

Levels of perfections:

1. Just by finding it you feel like you accomplished something
2. The staff is great. They have great Vietnamese smiles. Someone usually opens the door for you. They quickly bring you a menu and you there to take your order when you are ready.
3. They have great breakfasts, sandwiches, salads, desserts and drinks. The ingredients are top notch. They have great smoke salmon, bacon and roast beef. Three ingredients that suck most places in asia. 
4. Their wifi is excellent. I was able to stream movies without any issues. 
5. They have a cool eclectic shop that sells interesting items. Things from clothing, to moleskine notebooks, to trinkets and gadgets.

My only knock on the place is that their chairs are not very comfortable. If you want to work for a few hours your bum will be sore.

Saigon is hot. Staying out all day in the sun is not an option. This is a great place to go anytime of the day to relax and cool off. It is right in district 1 and near lots of the major attractions.

My favorite items on the menu are the smoked salmon and eggs...they come scrambled, but I get poached. A side of bacon is like 12 pieces...no kidding. Lastly, I love their roast beef salad.

The Dong Khoi strip tends to trap tourists and can be highly commercialised, tacky and overpriced. L'Usine is separated into two dining sections. Go for the second within the boutique - the ventilation is FAR BETTER than the section next to the open kitchen. There is also a nice alfresco terrace overlooking Dong Khoi with a great view of the Saigon Opera House - the best place for a strong iced coffee and a good book. The casual fusion menu has French leanings and offers some excellent breakfast options. We settled for some fresh juice (pomelo), pasta (vegetarian), soup (clam chowder), salad (grilled pork), baguette sandwiches (caramelised pork) to share. Competent food if your expectations are not sky high. Just-right portions with reasonable prices. Will be back for more.

Not to be missed: 
1. Amazing cupcakes for dessert or teatime. 
2. The boutique stocks very interesting and quality hipster fashions for he & she.
3. Chic industrial-inspired lighting fixtures for sale in the store.
Need to be improved:

L'Usine is what i would consider my ideal cafe. It is tucked away on the 2nd storey above a Vietnamese arts gallery. As i walked through the alley, what greeted me was a motorcycle parking garage which was kinda dodgy. Up the stairs i went and immediately i fell in love. This is quite similar to PS cafe but with a little more quirkiness.

High ceilings, open and airy space. Perfect place to while the afternoon away. Notice the similarities to PS? This is more relaxing i feel, people just leave you alone to do your own thing unlike in Sg where the servers make you feel you've overstayed your welcome. 

I love the long benches in the different sections of the cafe. Perfect for gatherings. Doesn't matter if you are sitting next to strangers. Who knows if they may become friends right? 

Took me some time to realize that i've been pushing such a huge door to get in and out of the cafe. Super woman!

Quirky wallpaper. Z thought it was a picture of some gentleman. I thought it was quite disturbing the first time i saw it. Then we realized it's actually Sun Wu Kong in a suit! This is not something i would have in my house though. Imagine those monkey eyes following you wherever you go. Shudders.

L'usine also has a retail space within the cafe. It feels very much like UO and looks exactly like an old warehouse. Love the natural light that filters in through the huge window panes and the little red bird cages from the wooden beamed ceilings. I bought a rubber watch (O clock) from italy and another foldable sports glasses from Sunpocket. Super cool stuff!

Finally onto the food. I can't say that i've tried much but their baked goods are out of this world. My favorite? CUPCAKES! The cupcakes are by Sweet + Sour and they are the moist-est thing you can find. I am no cupcake fan but i've fallen in love. Even the little cupcake place S brought me to in NYC couldn't beat this. I doubt Magnolia is as good. :P Great flavors- Chocolate, black and white, vanilla, choc-cinnamon etc. This is me eating my favorite flavour! Choc-caramel! 

This is the S'mores flavored one. Chocolate based cupcake with melted marshmallow top which is really creamy and light and not overpowering in sweetness. It has a hidden secret inside- graham swirls!!! How wonderful is that?

This is chocolate mint if i'm not wrong. Cute. But i'm not a choc mint fan so didn't try this.

The berry muffins are good too. Crusty muffin top with a moist interior and icing on top.

Cheese platter. Not sure what sort it is but both Z and i prefer soft cheese better. So creamy it spreads like condensed milk on the crackers. Yums.

Z likens the biscuit to 'Chicken in a biscuit'. Could try that for a cheese platter next time!

The red velvet is not very consistent though. The one time i tried it was dry but Z's was moist. Cream cheese frosting was good though. 

I was so hooked on the cupcakes i had to have them for desserts after dinner so we packed them. Our second hotel in Saigon was at Oscar Saigon and L'usine is just around the corner from there. Yay!

About my favorite choc-caramel- look carefully at the center! There's a chunk of melted caramel inside. It's like a kinder bueno. Love searching for treasures and surprises and the center is my favorite part. :))

Enjoying my cupcake in the comfort of our room. I finished 2 cupcakes on my own. Z didn't get much. :P 

This is how Bliss looks like. Or Contentment. Or maybe Gluttony. A bit unglamorous but honestly the tummy was doing a song and dance session right there and then. :)) If there's a reason why i'd fly to Saigon for a weekend trip it would be for the cupcakes. 

So if you are headed there, pop by L'usine. And get me a cupcake when you come back? Tyvm!!

Possibly the worst dining experience here at L'Usine. Waited for our food for 40 minutes, no one came to check why only 1 person has food. The order was wrong when it did come. Unapologetic manager unless you actually make a scene. Maybe they were busy with lunch crowd, but still not a good enough excuse. Long version below.

We arrived at 12pm, the place is decorated nicely and hip, caters to mainly the expat crowd. The place started filling up around that point. We ordered a long black and Vietnamese iced coffee while waiting for friend to show up. The long black was 1/2 of the cup and the Vietnamese iced coffee was only about 4 sips w/ a glass full of ice.

My friend came. We ordered 2 brekkie burgers and 1 quiche. My quiche came so I figured the burgers are not far behind. I waited to eat together. Then friends told me to go ahead. I had tentative bites. The burgers never showed up. i had about 1/2 of my quiche at this point. The other table that came after us got their burgers already. We were looking at diving photos, and no one came to check our orders.

At 12:45, we were hungry and getting frustrated in trying to get wait staff’s attention. I asked about the burgers and the staff said they are coming. Another 5 minutes went by, no burger. I asked to see the manager; the girl had the nerve to say no! I insisted on getting the manager, she said ok, ok. Another 5 minutes, no manager. So my friend and I went to find the manager. She was on the phone and very evasive, didn't even smile or acknowledge us. Still no food. Finally, she put down the phone and said she'll check the kitchen. at that time, the food came, however, no hollandais sauce. They only gave a little sloppy dish of ketchup. There was hollandais sauce on other people's leftover plate.

We pulled the manager over to our table, showed her there's no hollandais sauce. She hasn't apologized one bit at this point, just said she'll go check the kitchen. But she took another call before she went in. After she checked she said they've ran out the sauce. At this point, we were at the front of the room and my friend was getting a bit loud due to frustration. Then the manager started to apologize. We left our food untouched and walked out. At that point was 1pm and starving. So we went to our usual restaurant, Centro. The wait staff still remembered us from the last time I was there, which was 2 weeks ago.

Different but excellent food, especially the cakes!
May 2012 • Friends
Had lunch here with a friend who lives in Saigon. Not that easy to find, if you don't know where you are going.
It is an old warehouse that has been made into a smart cafe and shop.
The food for a lunchtime is excellent - sandwiches, salads. The shakes are among their with the best I had in Vietnam. I had a BBQ pulled pork baguette,my mouth is watering thinking about it!
Leave room for a cake, they are delicious!
You set at communal benches, which gives it a nice atmosphere. There are tables outside but I needed the air con! Not that cheap for Saigon but very different and good quality.
Have a look around the shop when you've finished eating. Some quirky things to buy.
Definitely worth a visit, if you can find it. Free wifi too
